the origin of egg-spots is a complex phenomenon that involves the expression of multiple genes and that the genetic mechanisms underlying the emergence of this trait are not conserved between the two major lineages of cichlid fish.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

egg-spots in cichlids are not homologous to blotches in cichlides and that the egg-spots in A. burtoni and C. pulpican share more similarity than the two types of egg-spots do with the blotches in P. philander and C. macrops.
the egg-spot trait has evolved in a highly conserved way in derived haplochromes, whereas the blotch trait has evolved in an independent way in ancestral haplochromes and ectodines.
egg-spots are a complex and novel trait, whereas blotches may be more ancient and simpler in their genetic basis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
egg-spots and other novel cichlid traits are likely to be underpinned by a complex genetic architecture.
egg-spots and other traits that have been shaped through sexual selection are likely to be controlled by different sets of genes than other traits that have evolved under other selective regimes.
the genetic basis of the novel traits egg-spots and anal blotches is likely to be complex and that a combination of genetic and phenotypic approaches is needed to unravel it.
